solution:
If \(|x|\le m\), then \(-m\le x\le m\).

Therefore

\(-3\le 4x-5\le 3\)

\(-3+5\le 4x\le 3+5\)

\(2\le 4x\le 8\)

\(\frac{2}{4}\le x\le \frac{8}{4}\)

\(\frac{1}{2}\le x\le 2\)

[Textbook error, answer-affecting: the printed solution correctly reaches \(|x| > 4\) and then states the COMPLEMENT of it, \(-4 < x < 4\), i.e. \(x \in (-4, 4)\). The correct domain is \((-\infty, -4) \cup (4, \infty)\). On the printed answer the function is undefined everywhere in the stated interval — at \(x = 0\), \(\bigl||0| - 1\bigr| - 3 = -2 < 0\).]

As function is defined for \(\big||x|-1\big|-3>0\)

Therefore \(\big||x|-1\big|>3\)

So \(|x|-1>3\) or \(|x|-1<-3\)

That is

\(|x|>3+1\) or \(|x|<-3+1\)

\(|x|>4\) or \(|x|<-2\)

But \(|x|<-2\) is not possible as \(|x|>0\) always

So \(-4<x<4\), \(x\in(-4,4)\).
_note: BOOK DEFECT (answer-affecting, last line of the printed solution). The solution correctly reduces to \(|x|>4\), which means \(x<-4\) or \(x>4\), i.e. domain \((-\infty,-4)\cup(4,\infty)\). The book instead prints \(-4<x<4\), \(x\in(-4,4)\) — the COMPLEMENT of the correct set, and a set on which the function is undefined everywhere (at \(x=0\), \(||0|-1|-3=-2<0\)). Every earlier line of the printed solution is correct; only the concluding line is wrong. Transcribed as printed per the brief.

solution:
Let \(f(x)=|x-1|+|x+2|\)

Here the critical points are at \(x=1\) and \(x=-2\).

They divide the number line into 3 parts, as follows.

| Region | Test Value | Sign | \(f(x)\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| I, \(x<-2\) | \(-3\) | \((x-1)<0\), \((x+2)<0\) | \(-(x-1)-(x+2)=-2x-1\) |
| II, \(-2\le x\le 1\) | \(0\) | \((x-1)<0\), \((x+2)>0\) | \(-(x-1)+(x+2)=3\) |
| III, \(x>1\) | \(2\) | \((x-1)>0\), \((x+2)>0\) | \((x-1)+(x+2)=2x+1\) |

As \(f(x)=8\)

From I, \(-2x-1=8\) \(\therefore -2x=9\) \(\therefore x=-\frac{9}{2}\).

From II, \(3=8\), which is impossible, hence there is no solution in this region.

From III, \(2x+1=8\) \(\therefore 2x=7\) \(\therefore x=\frac{7}{2}\).

Solutions are \(x=-\frac{9}{2}\) and \(x=\frac{7}{2}\).

The stem itself needs no figure — the sign chart supports the region table already transcribed in the solution.

stem: If \(\{x\}\) and \([x]\) are the fractional part function and greatest integer function of \(x\) respectively, solve for \(x\), if \(\{x+1\}+2x=4[x+1]-6\).
solution:
[Textbook error, answer-affecting: having found \([x] \in \{1, 2\}\) the book never substitutes back into its own equation \(3\{x\} = 2[x] - 2\); it simply unions the two intervals and prints \(x \in [1, 3)\). Substituting gives \(\{x\} = 0\) for \([x] = 1\) and \(\{x\} = \dfrac{2}{3}\) for \([x] = 2\), so the solution set is the two points \(\left\{1, \dfrac{8}{3}\right\}\). Counterexample against the printed interval: at \(x = 1.5\) the left side is \(3(0.5) = 1.5\) and the right side is \(2(1) - 2 = 0\).]

\(\{x+1\}+2x=4[x+1]-6\)

Since \(\{x+n\}=\{x\}\) and \([x+n]=[x]+n\), for \(n\in I\), also \(x=[x]+\{x\}\)

\(\therefore\;\{x\}+2(\{x\}+[x])=4([x]+1)-6\)

\(\therefore\;\{x\}+2\{x\}+2[x]=4[x]+4-6\)

\(\therefore\;3\{x\}=4[x]-2[x]-2\)

\(\therefore\;3\{x\}=2[x]-2\)  ... (I)

Since \(0\le\{x\}<1\)

\(\therefore\;0\le 3\{x\}<3\)

\(\therefore\;0\le 2[x]-2<3\)  \((\because\) from I\()\)

\(\therefore\;0+2\le 2[x]<3+2\)

\(\therefore\;2\le 2[x]<5\)

\(\therefore\;\frac{2}{2}\le[x]<\frac{5}{2}\)

\(\therefore\;1\le[x]<2.5\)

But as \([x]\) takes only integer values

\([x]=1,2\) since \([x]=1\Rightarrow 1\le x<2\) and \([x]=2\Rightarrow 2\le x<3\)

Therefore \(x\in[1,3)\)
_note:
COLUMN-WISE STRADDLE: stem, "Solution :" and the working down to \(1\le[x]<2.5\) are in the RIGHT column of p-20; the final three lines ("But as \([x]\) takes only integer values" ... "Therefore \(x\in[1,3)\)") continue at the TOP of the LEFT column of p-21. Transcribed whole.
BOOK DEFECT (answer-affecting, concluding lines). Having found \([x]\in\{1,2\}\), the book never substitutes back into its own equation (I) \(3\{x\}=2[x]-2\) to recover \(\{x\}\); it simply unions the two intervals \([x]=1\Rightarrow 1\le x<2\) and \([x]=2\Rightarrow 2\le x<3\) and prints \(x\in[1,3)\). Substituting gives \([x]=1\Rightarrow 3\{x\}=0\Rightarrow\{x\}=0\Rightarrow x=1\), and \([x]=2\Rightarrow 3\{x\}=2\Rightarrow\{x\}=\frac{2}{3}\Rightarrow x=\frac{8}{3}\). So the solution set is \(\{1,\frac{8}{3}\}\), two isolated points, not the interval \([1,3)\) — e.g. \(x=1.5\) lies in the printed answer but gives LHS \(=0.5+3=3.5\) and RHS \(=4(2)-6=2\). Transcribed as printed per the brief.
